title: Customer-scoped pseudonymization and expirable analytics views
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Provide a privacy-preserving analytics path that replaces raw PII with reversible or irreversible tokens depending on policy, exposes time-limited (expirable) materialized views for console consumers, and implements an auditable targeted purge workflow per customer. Scope includes: source ingestion transforms, a tokenization/pseudonymization microservice, expirable view generator for the ClickHouse/analytics store, a purge job orchestrator with SLA-aware retry/backoff, and audit logging for compliance. This work supports regulatory requirements (GDPR/CCPA) and internal data retention policies while minimizing disruption to console dashboards and cost-sensitive reporting jobs. Constraints: must support existing streaming pipelines (Kafka -> stream processors -> analytical store), maintain <5% additional end-to-end latency for real-time pipelines, and avoid doubling storage costs for analytics snapshots. Success metrics: (1) All PII in analytics stream either pseudonymized or removed within 24 hours of ingestion, (2) 0 console dashboard breakages for top-10 queries after rollout, (3) targeted purge completes for a single-customer 6 months of events within SLA (24 hours) with verifiable audit record.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming ingestion applies configured pseudonymization profiles to fields classified as PII without dropping non-PII telemetry
Expirable materialized views are created per-customer with TTL policy and expire automatically once policy elapses
Purge orchestrator can queue and execute targeted purges that remove both raw and derived artifacts and emits an immutable audit record
Integration tests demonstrating console dashboards render correctly against pseudonymized views for representative queries
End-to-end benchmark showing <5% increase in pipeline latency and <15% storage overhead for snapshots
Security review completed and tokenization KMS integration validated
implementation_steps: Design pseudonymization policy DSL and map to schema fields (PM + Privacy Eng)
Implement tokenization microservice with KMS-backed reversible tokens and optionally irreversible hashing modes
Add transform stage to streaming processors (Fluent/StreamZ) to call tokenization service or apply hash depending on policy
Implement expirable materialized view generator in analytics orchestrator (creates per-customer views with retention TTL and metadata tags)
Build purge orchestrator: job queue (Rabbit/Kafka), planner to find affected tables/partitions/derived artifacts, worker with safe-delete primitives
Wire audit events to immutable append-only store (signed events + certificate thumbprint) and surface in Console for compliance team
Create migration tool for backfilling existing data per policy with throttling and verification
Add observability: per-customer purge progress, rate-limits, error classifications, SLO dashboards
Run canary on internal customer telemetry, iterate based on metrics and QA findings, then roll to first customer cohort
test_plan: Unit tests for tokenization service covering reversible and irreversible modes
Integration tests: Kafka -> Stream processor -> tokenization -> analytics store using synthetic PII datasets
Property-based tests ensuring pseudonymization is deterministic when reversible tokens are used and non-reversible when hashing mode selected
End-to-end acceptance: create expirable view, query console endpoints, then expire view and verify safe fallback
Purge dry-run: run orchestrator in dry-run mode to emit list of affected objects, validate against expected targets
Chaos test: simulate partial failures in tokenization service and verify pipeline backpressure and retry semantics
data_migrations: Backfill job to pseudonymize historical payloads: batched map-reduce over ClickHouse partitions by customer id
Metadata migration: attach retention tags and policy id to existing materialized views and tables
Archive raw payloads beyond retention into cold storage prior to irreversible deletion to support legal holds
observability: Metrics: pseudonymization throughput (records/sec), error rate, average tokenization latency
Dashboards: per-customer pending purge count, purge throughput, purge failure reasons
Audit trail: immutable event viewer with filters by customer, action, operator, timestamp
Alerts: purge job failures >5% or purges exceeding SLA window (24h) trigger P0 pager
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Dashboard queries break when fields are tokenized. Mitigation: provide schema-mapped lookup functions backed by reversible tokens for safe-join operations and run query compatibility tests for top-10 dashboards.
Risk: Performance regression in streaming path. Mitigation: batch tokenization calls, implement local LRU cache for recent tokens, and provide an opt-out fast-hash mode for low-sensitivity customers.
Risk: Incomplete purge of derived artifacts. Mitigation: maintain lineage map for common derived tables and run verification passes that compare counts before/after purge in a sandbox environment.
Risk: Legal hold requests. Mitigation: retain an append-only archive path and flag records to exempt from irreversible deletion until hold is cleared.

Risk: Key compromise for reversible tokens. Mitigation: rotate KMS keys with forward compatibility and keep a key-access audit log; require security review before reversible mode enabled for a customer
